solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Perhaps U-boat, with German, to surrender

parts.note: a U-boat is an example of a sub, short for submarine
mit is the German word for 'with'

explanation.surface: A German U-boat crew giving itself up to the enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: To submit is to yield to another's authority, a synonym of giving oneself up.

clue.text: Polish initially reviled in The Sun?

parts.note: to shine shoes is to polish them

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so just the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A Polish person attacked in The Sun tabloid newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality and 'The Sun' like the British tabloid, but the Sun here is the star, something that gives off light.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun is something that beams, a light-giver; the question mark marks it as an example.

indicators.note: after means the second piece follows the first in the answer

parts.note: a bug is a minor illness such as a stomach bug
to stomach something is to bear or tolerate it

explanation.surface: A bad night's dreams brought on by stomach trouble after being ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear is a persistent source of dread or annoyance, a figurative bad dream.

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Pubs and hotels found at both ends of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostelries are places offering lodging and drink to travellers, like taverns.

indicators.note: to shackle is to hold something fast within restraints, so the first name holds the artist inside it

parts.note: Kate is the usual short form of the name Catherine
RA, Royal Academician, is the standard crossword artist

explanation.surface: A woman named Catherine restrains a painter while playing some game.
explanation.definitionFit: Karate is a Japanese martial art practised competitively, so it counts as a sport.

clue.text: Some characters moving a table outside pub

indicators.note: outside means the shuffled letters sit around the abbreviation, enclosing it
moving the letters shifts them around into a new order

parts.note: PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub

explanation.surface: People shifting a table out of a pub on the pavement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' shuffles A TABLE into ALABET, and 'outside' wraps it round PH.
explanation.definitionFit: Characters here are letters; the full set used to write a language contains some of them.

clue.text: Titan hiding in downbeat LA suburb

indicators.note: something hiding in these words is concealed within their letters, running across them

explanation.surface: A giant of a man lying low in a gloomy Los Angeles suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, Atlas was a Titan condemned to hold up the sky.

parts.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
to nurse a patient is to tend them

explanation.surface: A one-time nurse receiving a job offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend an invitation or hand is to hold it out, to proffer it.

indicators.note: letters arranged strangely are put in an unexpected new order

explanation.surface: An inexperienced young woman who is, oddly enough, the real thing.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingénue is a naive, innocent young woman, especially such a role on stage.

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, as seed is sown, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A Londoner on television mocked as a programme goes out.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a BBC soap opera set in London's East End, home of the cockney; a character in it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A character from the BBC soap set in London's East End is a television Londoner, a cockney.

clue.text: Scheme to involve one expert at banking?

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so the scheme takes the numeral inside it

parts.note: a plot is a secret scheme
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A plan drawn up to bring in a financial specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banking' suggests money, but here it is an aircraft tilting as it turns; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who flies aircraft must be skilled at tilting them into turns, the aviation sense of banking.

clue.text: First wife and knight on terms

parts.note: Eve, in Genesis, was Adam's wife and the first woman
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: The first woman and a knight getting along with each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Being level, neither ahead nor behind, is being on equal terms with someone.

clue.text: One kills when elite troops stray from path

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
the SAS, Special Air Service, is Britain's elite special forces regiment
to sin is to stray from the path of righteousness

explanation.surface: Special forces who wander off course end up killing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired or political murderer is one whose job is to kill.

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
in cricket a paceman is a bowler who relies on speed

explanation.surface: A slight cricketer whose fast bowling seems jet-powered.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler delivers the ball to the batsman; a fast bowler is called a paceman.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut is carried into orbit by a rocket, so is someone propelled by one.

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
present means here, in attendance

explanation.surface: A stage show playing at this very venue.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent something is to depict or portray it, a sense of show.

indicators.note: windy suggests twisting and winding, so the letters wind about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling that the weather is far too blustery.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a violent whirlwind is certainly very windy.
explanation.definitionFit: A twister is a violent rotating windstorm, the extreme case of windy weather.

clue.text: Order to begin shooting in battle

definitions.meaning: the word a film director calls to start the cameras rolling
fighting, as in soldiers killed in combat

explanation.surface: A command to start firing in the midst of combat.
explanation.definitionFit: A director calls for cameras to roll with this word, and it also means military combat.

indicators.note: exploding blows the word apart so its letters land in a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An instruction to boil these until they burst with energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that seethes bubbles and foams, as when it is on the boil.

clue.text: Agree money taken by party as reported

parts.note: coin is money in metal form

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the pieces are judged by how they sound

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute or contest

explanation.surface: A deal is agreed once a political party has taken some cash, so the press says.
explanation.definitionFit: Two accounts that coincide match each other exactly, so they correspond or concur.

clue.text: Turned over papers brought to light

indicators.note: brought to means the first piece is placed up against the next one, which follows it

parts.note: ID, identification, is a person's papers
an LED, light-emitting diode, is a small electric light

explanation.surface: Documents uncovered and revealed to the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned over' looks like flipping papers, but it is an engine running at rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine ticking over without moving the car is running in neutral, so it idled.

indicators.note: some of the word means only part of its letters are taken, a run inside it

explanation.surface: A fried egg placed on top of a few burgers.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to encourage or spur them, the same as to press them.

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: gums stick things together, so to gum is to stick

explanation.surface: Someone stands up for a person who thinks himself above others.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-satisfied person acts superior, pleased with themselves and condescending.

clue.text: African country about to embrace second religion

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within one's arms, so the country holds the letter inside it
about here means turned round, so the name of the country is read backwards

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
s is the abbreviation for second, as in time

explanation.surface: An African nation is said to be on the point of adopting a second faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to embrace' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' turns MALI into ILAM, which then takes S inside.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the monotheistic faith of Muslims, founded on the Koran, one of the world's major religions.

clue.text: Unrestrained, a politician breaks into bombast

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so the pieces go within the tirade

parts.note: a rant is loud, overblown, bombastic talk
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A politician bursts into a pompous speech without holding back.
explanation.definitionFit: Rampant means running wild, growing or spreading without check.

indicators.note: a name mistaken is muddled, so its letters come out in a wrong order

parts.note: the name as printed has one N; the anagram needs the spelling Dianne, with a second N, to give six letters

explanation.surface: Someone called Diane is taken for a different woman.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, Diane has five letters and only one N, so it cannot give a six-letter answer; the anagram works only from the spelling Dianne.
explanation.definitionFit: Nadine is a female first name, so it is a different woman's name from Diane.

indicators.note: denied its introduction means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: signore is the Italian for a man or gentleman, as in Mr

explanation.surface: An Italian gentleman snubbed by being refused an introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun someone is to pay them no heed, to cold-shoulder them deliberately.
